101958.notes: Method 1. princeinstitute.edu own-site notice: 'Prince Institute closed on March 17, 2017' with a records table. Wind-down was long and public: captures through 2014-06-18 show a normal recruiting homepage; the 2014-07-01 capture says 'Prince Institute is no longer enrolling new students... our two campus locations in Schaumburg, Illinois and Montgomery, Alabama are open and remain committed to educating and mentoring our existing students'; by 2016 both campuses were run from administrative offices in Elmhurst (this unit's IPEDS address). 'announced' left null because the 2014 notice announced the end of enrolment, not an explicit closure; a coder may treat 2014-06 as the announcement. The Southeast unit is the Montgomery, AL campus administered from Elmhurst. IPEDS close 03/16/2017 matches.

105163.recordsNote: No pre-closure custody agreement found. Electronic transcripts for 2001+ graduates via Parchment; hard-copy files claimed by the Chapter 7 trustee (ITT Educational Services estate, S.D. Ind.); some states later recovered records through litigation/settlement (MHEC 2018, Texas 2018 settlement).
105163.notes: Chain-wide shutdown of ITT Educational Services on 2016-09-06, announced the same day, effective immediately; Chapter 7 filed 2016-09-16. ED had barred new Title IV enrollments on 2016-08-25, and ITT said on 2016-08-30 it would let current students finish, so students had effectively no notice. teachOut coded n/a under SHEEO's 'abrupt, no plan possible'; Mass. BHE says no teach-out or transfer options were offered (ED offered closed-school discharge or credit transfer, and some states arranged transfer pathways afterward). IPEDS close dates of 2017-09-03 (Boise, Fort Wayne, St Petersburg; Nashville is in the Tennessee group) and 2016-09-06 (Oak Brook, Orland Park, Springfield IL) are reporting-cycle artifacts: ITT ceased all operations in Sept 2016 (Fort Wayne confirmed individually by Indiana CHE). Boise and St Petersburg were not individually confirmed, they are assumed within the chain-wide closure. 'closed' date is the instruction-cessation date; ED's formal Title IV eligibility loss followed the bankruptcy (2016-09-16). Merger coded none: no acquirer or buyer identified in sources read.

evidence.claim: Official ED page: on September 6, 2016 ITT Technical Institutes announced closing its 130+ campuses; Chapter 7 petition filed September 16, 2016 (S.D. Ind.); all ITT Technical Institutes lost Title IV eligibility.
ED email to students dated Sept 6, 2016: students affected by the announcement of closure of the institution on September 6, 2016; options were closed school loan discharge or credit transfer.

Massachusetts BHE: ITT 'suddenly announced the closure of all of its campuses' on Sept 6, 2016; all instruction ceased as of Sept 6; 'no teach-out period or transfer options were offered to students'; student-record location/availability still argued in Chapter 7.
Indiana CHE fact sheet: ITT announced closure Sept 6, 2016 and closed all 136 locations including Fort Wayne and South Bend.

Aug 25, 2016 ED bar on new Title IV enrollments; Aug 30 ITT said current students could finish; Sept 6 announced closing all campuses 'effective immediately'; Sept 16 Chapter 7. No campus sale or acquirer described.
California BPPE: informed that all ITT Tech schools are closing (emails sent Sept 6, 2016); directs transcript requests to Parchment.

Dec 2015 Durbin letter reports Westwood said it would teach out/end operations at many campuses incl. its four Illinois campuses. Closure announced to students by email ~2016-01-25 (Wikipedia, citing the school email); press reported it 2016-01-27 (CBS Colorado, Inside Higher Ed 'announced Wednesday'); so announced date coded to month. January 2016 term was the last term; campuses closed by 2016-03-08 (ABC7, Wikipedia citing Westwood's 2016-03-29 acknowledgment of closure of all campuses effective 2016-03-08). Abrupt=false is a judgment: roughly six weeks of notice plus partner-school transfer path (credits accepted at same or lower tuition; transfer deadline 2016-02-19), but no formal teach-out found, Westwood acknowledged credits generally would not transfer, and ABC7 reports students were told they could finish at Westwood before being told to transfer (students 'scrambling'); a reviewer could reasonably code this abrupt or teachOut 'no'. Records custodian not established from pages I could read (IBHE pages, which a search summary said point to Parchment for transcripts, were unreachable; not verified). Per-campus differences not checked beyond Illinois/Colorado coverage. Wikipedia's campus list also names Houston campuses not in this batch.

I could not fetch a page that names Cheyenne, Cincinnati, Columbus OH, Delaware, Springfield, Wichita or Omaha: Springfield (SBJ) and Cincinnati/West Chester (Journal-News) phase-outs appeared only in search snippets of pages that returned 403/429, and no 2012 campus list was found. Omaha closing in 2014 is the least certain. Closed dates left null.

10-Q Feb 2014: ~three-fourths of the 115 locations closed; remaining closures continue through FY2014 and beyond as regulatory approvals are obtained and teach-out obligations completed.

448521.name: University of Phoenix-Omaha Campus

448530.mergerNote: Folded into another University of Phoenix reporting unit (state-level unit or University of Phoenix-Arizona); same institution, no outside party.
448530.notes: IPEDS flags these units 'combined' into a state-level University of Phoenix unit (or Arizona for Online/Phoenix/Southern Arizona), mostly in 2014; Eastern Washington was combined into the Online Campus in 2010. University of Phoenix is a single HLC-accredited institution that reports many campuses (FY2014 10-K), so this is read as a reporting restructure, not an institutional closure; no non-IPEDS source describing the 2014 restructure was found, hence low confidence. SHEEO closure fields left null because they apply only to closures. Caveats: individual campuses in this list may have physically closed on their own timeline, either under the Oct 2012 plan to close 115 locations (a WTOC item names 'the Columbus campus' and the Atlanta learning center as closing, probably Columbus GA = unit 443881) or later in 2017-2024; this group does not describe those physical closures. Search budget ran out before per-campus checks were possible.

evidence.claim: FY2014 10-K: University of Phoenix is regionally accredited by HLC as one institution operating ~110 ground campus locations; the plan to close 115 locations began FY2013 (context for single-institution structure; does not itself describe the IPEDS reporting change).
10-Q Feb 2014: location closures in the FY2013 plan are continuing through FY2014 and beyond (context that some campuses here may have closed physically).

448530.name: University of Phoenix-Northwest Arkansas Campus

448549.notes: Assumes the 'Northwest Indiana Campus' is the Merrillville campus (8401 Ohio St). Local business paper (Oct 31 2012) reports Merrillville closing in the national shutdown, about 200 students affected, impact on them 'still being determined', no new students enrolled. IPEDS flags the unit 'combined' into University of Phoenix-Indiana in 2012, so the IPEDS change and the physical closure may be separate. Closed date left null.

evidence.claim: Oct 31 2012: Merrillville campus closing as part of the nationwide shutdown; ~200 students affected, impact still being determined; no new students enrolled.
Oct 22 2012: national plan announced; affected students may continue online or at alternative sites.

448549.name: University of Phoenix-Northwest Indiana Campus

448558.notes: Madison campus confirmed on the October 2012 closure list (Madison, Brookfield, Grand Chute). About 150 students could finish through graduation, possibly at a different location. evidence.claim: Oct 19 2012: University of Phoenix will stop enrolling new students and eventually close Madison, Brookfield and Grand Chute campuses; ~150 Madison students can finish through graduation though location may change.
Oct 22 2012: Apollo announced closing 115 locations (25 main campuses) before end of 2013; affected students can continue online, at alternative on-ground sites or existing locations.

448558.name: University of Phoenix-Madison Campus

448567.notes: State-level University of Phoenix reporting units whose IPEDS records close 2016-2021 as the last ground campus in the state finished teach-out; University of Phoenix continues online, so students were not displaced from the institution. No unit-specific announcement or teach-out source was found (search budget exhausted), so announced is null and abrupt/teachOut rest on the university's documented program-wide practice of teach-out and online continuation (2012 plan, Sept 2017 wave, 2021 phase-out). Massachusetts (Braintree) is separated out with its own source. Illinois: Illinois Board of Higher Education closed-school notice (found only as a search snippet; page fetch failed) says UoP moved all instruction online and ceased operating as an independent institution in Illinois as of June 30 2021, which conflicts with the IPEDS date of 06/13/2019. Georgia and Utah: Wikipedia says UoP closed the Atlanta and Salt Lake City campuses in 2021. Some units here may belong to the Sept 2017 wave or the Oct 2012 plan; unverified. Closed dates left null.

evidence.claim: 10-Q Feb 2014: location closures proceed as UoP obtains regulatory approvals and completes teach-out obligations for campuses not yet closed.
Sept 2017: UoP instituting a teach-out phase at campuses and centers; current students not affected, no new students admitted.
Apr 2022: a campus stops operating once all its students have moved online or finished required in-person coursework; closures began as early as 2016.
UoP history: Oct 2024 completed planned and approved teach-out and closure of all ground campuses except Phoenix.

448567.name: University of Phoenix-South Carolina

448576.notes: Dream Center Education Holdings (owner of Argosy University and the Art Institutes) confirmed on Mon 2 Jul 2018 that it would stop enrolling new students at 30 campuses including San Bernardino CA; BPPE/OSAR logged notice of possible closure on 2 Jul 2018. Wikipedia says 23 Art Institutes closed in Dec 2018 and lists Inland Empire among closed/sold campuses; IPEDS close date 12/14/2018 is used as the stand-in (closed left null). Note a BPPE emergency order of March 2019 still lists 'Art Institute of California - Inland Empire (Satellite)' as an approved Argosy location, which may just be licensing records; the broader DCEH collapse (receivership, Title IV cut off 27 Feb 2019, all remaining campuses ceased instruction 8 Mar 2019) may have affected students here. The July 2018 announcement was an enrollment halt, not explicitly a closure date. I did not find a campus-specific teach-out, abruptness, or records custodian (transcripts for DCEH schools were routed via Parchment and the Arizona State Board for Private Postsecondary Education per Maryland MHEC, but that is system-wide, not confirmed for California). Merger: EDMC sold the Art Institutes/Argosy to the nonprofit Dream Center in Oct-Nov 2017, which is a parent-level sale, not coded.

evidence.claim: 3 Jul 2018: company spokeswoman confirmed on Monday that 30 campuses including Art Institute San Bernardino CA stopped accepting new students; active students to continue classes; no formal teach-out described.

California OSAR received notice on 2 Jul 2018 that Art Institute of California (incl. San Bernardino) and Argosy campuses may be closing; page updated 15 Aug 2018; no closure date, teach-out or custodian listed.
In December 2018, 23 Art Institutes were closed; Art Institute of California-Inland Empire listed under closed or sold campuses with no date.

Some DCEH institutions ceased instruction 8 Mar 2019; transcripts requested through Parchment and the Arizona State Board for Private Postsecondary Education; teach-outs described are Maryland-specific.

448576.name: Argosy University-The Art Institute of California-Inland Empire

448628.mergerNote: No sale or merger found; Sen. Durbin (Dec 2015) said Alta might seek to sell some campuses, but all campuses closed 2016-03-08 and no buyer is reported.
448628.notes: Parent: Alta Colleges Inc. (ACICS-accredited). Enrollment suspended chain-wide 2015-11-11/12 (not itself a closure announcement). Dec 2015 Durbin letter reports Westwood said it would teach out/end operations at many campuses incl. its four Illinois campuses. Closure announced to students by email ~2016-01-25 (Wikipedia, citing the school email); press reported it 2016-01-27 (CBS Colorado, Inside Higher Ed 'announced Wednesday'); so announced date coded to month. January 2016 term was the last term; campuses closed by 2016-03-08 (ABC7, Wikipedia citing Westwood's 2016-03-29 acknowledgment of closure of all campuses effective 2016-03-08). Abrupt=false is a judgment: roughly six weeks of notice plus partner-school transfer path (credits accepted at same or lower tuition; transfer deadline 2016-02-19), but no formal teach-out found, Westwood acknowledged credits generally would not transfer, and ABC7 reports students were told they could finish at Westwood before being told to transfer (students 'scrambling'); a reviewer could reasonably code this abrupt or teachOut 'no'. Records custodian not established from pages I could read (IBHE pages, which a search summary said point to Parchment for transcripts, were unreachable; not verified). Per-campus differences not checked beyond Illinois/Colorado coverage. Wikipedia's campus list also names Houston campuses not in this batch.

evidence.claim: Enrollment suspended 2015-11-12; email to students 2016-01-25 that college would close in March after January term; all 15 campuses closed effective 2016-03-08 per Westwood's 2016-03-29 acknowledgment; transfer options to partner schools but no formal teach-out described; owner Alta Colleges Inc.
Closure reported 2016-01-27: campuses close in March at end of semester; students told to choose a partner school by mid-February.

Emails told students they must transfer by 2016-02-19; January 2016 term last term; campuses close by March 8; partner schools agreed to accept credits at same or lower tuition; enrollment stopped 2015-11-11; students said they had been told they could finish at Westwood.
Westwood announced (Wednesday, 2016-01-27) it will shut down in March; stopped enrolling in November; no teach-out/transfer detail.
2015-12-14: Alta suspended enrollment 2015-11-12; Westwood will teach out and end operations at many campuses incl. four Illinois campuses and may seek to sell others (attempted sale not confirmed).

448628.name: Westwood College-Annandale

448655.notes: Kaplan Higher Education announced on 2012-09-28 a plan to stop enrolling at nine campuses and consolidate four others, but did not name them; I could not find a campus-specific source for Denver (Thornton), Cincinnati, Columbus, Milwaukee, Stockton or Midland. They are grouped because all are on Kaplan's closed-college list and their IPEDS exit dates (2012-11 to 2013-09) fit the teach-out window of that plan. Membership in the nine is inferred, so announced/abrupt left null and teachOut reflects only the company-level written statement. Midland's IPEDS record carries a Lubbock city. Individual campuses can deviate from the plan (see Chesapeake). Human check recommended: local news or state regulator (CO DHE, OH SBCCS, WI EAB, CA BPPE, TX TWC) for per-campus notice dates.

evidence.claim: FY2012 10-K: 'On September 27, 2012, KHE finalized a plan to consolidate its market presence at certain of its fixed-facility campuses'; KHE ceased new enrollments at nine ground campuses and will consolidate four other campuses into nearby locations; KHE will continue to teach courses in progress at these campuses until completion. Campuses are not named.

FY2013 10-K: under the plan KHE ceased new enrollments at nine ground campuses and consolidated four others; KHE has taught and will continue to teach all courses in progress until completion; at end of 2013 courses remained in progress at only two locations.
Inside Higher Ed (2012-09-30): Kaplan announced Friday 2012-09-28 that it will close nine campuses (unnamed); enrolled students may finish their courses but no new students enrolled.
Kaplan's closed-colleges page lists this campus among 41 closed colleges whose records are maintained by Kaplan North America; campuses not listed were acquired by ECA (renamed Brightwood).

448655.name: Kaplan College-Milwaukee

448664.notes: Inferred from context: Delta/Miller-Motte began closing campuses in late 2017 after ACCET rejection and ACICS loss of recognition; these five IPEDS-closed units (Madison TN 12/24/2017; Greenville NC, Clarksville TN, Lynchburg VA, Roanoke VA all 05/25/2018) are absent from Ancora's Jan 2018 purchase list and from the current campus list. The seven campuses that stopped enrolling in Sept 2017 were never named in sources I could read, so membership of these five in that list is unconfirmed; the WKRN Sept 4, 2017 report ('plans to end enrollment at 7 locations') returned 403. Shared 05/25/2018 IPEDS date suggests a common wind-down end date. Abrupt not coded: ending new enrollment ~8 months before the IPEDS date suggests orderly with continuing students, but no teach-out or transfer arrangement was found. Announced date not coded because campuses are unconfirmed (candidate: 2017-09). Madison's 12/24/2017 date looks like a year-end IPEDS stand-in.

450207.notes: Chain-wide shutdown of ITT Educational Services on 2016-09-06, announced the same day, effective immediately; Chapter 7 filed 2016-09-16. NBC 6, 2016-10-19: Perez charged with two misdemeanor counts of improper school closure for closing both Dade Medical College and USMF in October 2015 without warning; state law requires 30 days' notice to CIE and a plan for students to finish or transfer records; students and faculty were emailed one hour before closure.

Colorado Springs South and Richardson are in the batch but are coded separately because they kept ground students into 2019.
